_method_note: Structured cross-references between locations, time periods, characters, and concepts found across the material set. Every entry lists its source file(s). Nothing here is asserted beyond what a source states; where sources disagree, both values are kept and a matching entry is added to 'conflicts'. Full prose per source lives in material/_context.md; this file is the associative index. Sources are abbreviated: atlax_i, atlax_ii, catastro, ensayo_i, libro, timelines_py (timelines.py), esquema (ESQUEMA.pdf), book_of_inventions, cartography_highways/cartography_trains/cartography_airports (Cartography (Map Markers) [Code].xlsx), luminacion_register (Luminacion Register [Code].xlsx), mapa_del_milenio (El Antiguo Continente de Milkan - Mapa del Milenio.png), plus 5 dated/named screenshots (Khan Ice WP, Sid Nalta WP, Milka General Map, Milka Oceans Plan and Continent Outline, Ruta Lundria-Salthos Cruzados) referenced inline by filename. Per the user (2026-07-24), 'Luminacion Register' and 'Terraforming Regions Purge Register.xlsx' ARE lore sources, split into a narrative layer (named characters/locations/actions - captured under characters.named_inhabitants) and a technical/'mysterious formula' layer (Clock-worldTime triggers, Taterzen movement logic, region-purge flags - left undeciphered, see unknown.md) - not excluded, just not yet interpreted. Some conflict entries also carry a 'user_resolution' field: a design decision the user gave directly (not derived from any document), dated. These sit alongside the documentary facts rather than replacing them. IMPORTANT: everything above this line, and everything in 'locations'/'time_systems'/'routes'/'characters'/'concepts'/'conflicts' below, is the OBJECTIVE record - reconstructed from primary materials, per the archaeologist method. A second, SUBJECTIVE record sits alongside it: the top-level 'hearsay' array near the end of this file, mirroring _lore/hearsay/hearsay.md, logging what characters have actually said in played Blabber dialogues - never merged into the objective arrays above and never treated as corroborating them, even when they happen to agree; see 'hearsay._method_note' for the exact shape, including how a claim's consistency with the record and with facts is tracked. A third, OBJECTIVE-track array (not subjective like 'hearsay') is 'tales', fed by the /tell skill and mirrored in _lore/tale/: told/stated directly by the user, the world's author, folded into locations/characters/concepts/routes/time_systems via a 'tale:<id>' source tag, and into 'conflicts' on disagreement, by the same rules as any material source; see that array's own _method_note for the exact shape, including 'told_by' vs 'responsible'. Update (2026-07-26): 'ensayo_i_final' is a later, July 2026 edition of ensayo_i ('ENSAYO I (Final Version).pdf'), by the same credited author under an expanded byline ('Iläria Astraëa desde la lejana ciudad de Lündria'). Where the two editions disagree, both are kept, per the same disagreement rule as every other source pair - see CONFLICT-15, CONFLICT-16, CONFLICT-17.

hearsay._method_note: SUBJECTIVE record, distinct from every array above. Mirrors _lore/characters/hearsay.md exactly - one entry per real (non-template) dialog file in data/luminacion/blabber/dialogues/. 'claims' are what a character asserted, not verified facts; 'about' cross-references an id in 'locations'/'concepts'/'conflicts' above ONLY to mark topical overlap, never as corroboration. Consistency is recorded INCONSISTENT-ONLY: a field is present on a claim only when a genuine contradiction was actually found; absence means either 'checked and matches' or 'nothing to check against yet' - recording the unremarkable case explicitly on every claim would just be noise. Two independent flags: (1) 'inconsistent_with_record', an array of {about, source_kind, note} objects - present only when the claim contradicts something in the objective arrays above ('about' names the contradicted entry/CONFLICT id, 'source_kind' is 'material'/'tale' naming which of the two kinds of objective source the contradicted entry rests on, since disbelieving a written map and disbelieving something someone was told directly are different in kind - a character might reasonably distrust one and not the other; 'note' explains the contradiction in one sentence). (2) 'inconsistent_with_facts', a plain string (present only when true, value = the explanation) - set when a claim contradicts one of the two universal facts in _lore/facts/facts.json. No 'fact_ref' id is needed: there are only two facts, they are baked into every character unconditionally, and checking against them means reading facts.json directly, not looking up an id. A claim can also surface a genuine gap rather than a contradiction - something the objective record has never addressed at all, not something it disagrees with; when that happens and it resonates with the existing corpus, log it in _lore/unknown.md (cross-referencing the claim's id), matching the file's existing shape, the same way material and tale do. Not every claim produces one - skip rather than manufacturing a question that isn't genuinely there. Since scripts/sample_lore_knowledge.py draws individual claims from this array into a character's knowledge pool at the same odds as any objective-record fact (see README §8 Step 1), a claim can now be retold by a new character and logged again as a fresh claim. Whenever that happens, scripts/lineage_coin.py rolls a flat 50/50 to decide whether the origin survives the retelling: 'traceable' sets 'derived_from' (a claim id, e.g. 'nawom_morkulo_first_meeting#5') and the dialog line may cite the source by name; 'untraceable' leaves 'derived_from' unset and sets 'oral_lore': true instead - no origin recorded, dialog line uses vague framing ('they say...'), regardless of whether the content itself has drifted. 'oral_lore' can also be set true (paired with a 'note' explaining what grew) on a claim that traces back fine but has still accumulated specifics beyond what its 'about' grounding supports. Most claims have none of these fields - they're unremarkable, either freshly sampled from the objective record or a faithful, traceable retelling.

claims.note: Untraceable lineage_coin.py roll: Bardaglis holds ilaria_espiral_de_la_historia#3 but could name no source, so derived_from stays unset and the line says as much out loud. Unusually, the claim is then confirmed firsthand by its own subject in the same breath, which is far stronger grounding than the retelling had.

claims.text: Ilaria says there is another book covering the same centuries differently, that the two do not agree, and that she would rather have two accounts that contradict each other than one that sounds whole.
claims.note: She names herself as the author of one of the two, which is what makes her refusal to adjudicate between them costly rather than neutral.

claims.text: Bardaglis refuses to put their own name to their song while insisting Khaoe's line keeps hers - theirs was made to leave, hers got away from her.
claims.note: The distinction is the whole of Bardaglis's position: the standard applies to what they made, not to what they carry for other people.

claims.text: The Cordillera de Eurasori adorns the northern border of Khan Icé and was said to have been raised by gods, possibly Eurasori himself, sculpted by hands inspired by the creators' worlds.

claims.text: The taiga biome with cherry forests mixes elements of Khan Icé and Plathinëa. Cherry trees were used as diplomatic and ceremonial gifts by Dragón, with small saplings planted in friendly cities.
Cherry trees from Dragón are found in almost every city Milkucha has visited.

claims.text: The Desert of Experimentation was the first desert, a vast zone where redstone inventions were tested and eventually abandoned.
The Desert of Balahm is the land of temples.

entries.summary: Farlis, from Görff and a member of the Collective, visits Auroboro III's alcoba. Their disagreement is immediate: Auroboro III clings to military glory and ancestral honor; Farlis sees those wars as a hierarchy to be rejected, not preserved. The clash is fundamental — about memory, about what deserves to be kept.

claims.text: Farlis claims the Guerras de Görff were merely officers and nobles fighting over borders—a hierarchy-struggle, not heroic sacrifice. Auroboro III's ancestors meant more than that.
claims.note: Auroboro III's interpretation: Farlis reduces genuine ancestral honor to political power-struggle. Refusal to see the valor in the wars. Mutated through rejection of Farlis's radical reframing.

claims.text: Auroboro III argues that without memory, people are adrift and lose identity. Farlis counters that he knows who he is—someone who builds real things, not someone trapped talking about ghosts.
claims.note: Core collision between preservation and rejection. Each sees the other as trapped: Auroboro in nostalgia, Farlis in denial of the past's value.

claims.text: Farlis is from Görff and a member of the Collective, which dismantled the old military families and their hierarchy. Auroboro III sees this as erasure; Farlis sees it as liberation.
claims.note: Ideological divide: Auroboro mutates this as 'radical destruction of heritage'; Farlis mutates it as 'necessary dismantling of oppression.'

claims.text: Auroboro III believes honoring the Guerras means keeping his ancestors alive, not forgetting them. Farlis sees the alcoba as a man sitting alone with his ghosts, refusing to move forward.
claims.note: Auroboro's mutation: his work is life-giving memory-keeping. Farlis's mutation: his work is sterile nostalgia. Same act, opposite framings.

tales._method_note: A THIRD kind of source, distinct from both the objective record above and 'hearsay' - see _lore/tale/_index.md. Deliberately not distinguishing those two framings with a fact/fiction label: a tale can be partly true, the way a real legend often is, and that ambiguity is the point. Unlike hearsay, a tale IS folded into the objective arrays above (locations/characters/concepts/routes/time_systems) wherever it overlaps an existing entry - via a 'tale:<id>' item added to that entry's 'sources' list, exactly like a material-file abbreviation - never by overwriting an existing entry. 'told_by' (nullable) names who is credited IN-FICTION with this tale, if it's framed that way (a character, an institution, a legend) - both a name and 'nobody' are genuine, deliberate answers; most tales leave it null since there's usually no in-world frame at all. entries.summary: Peregrins are itinerant holy pilgrims, hundreds of years into a tradition of setting out yearly to encounter every temple in the world in search of 'the diverse divinity.' Bound by a vow of understanding and peace, they travel land, sea, and air, renouncing their own identity to become a canvas onto which the world's cultures express themselves and endure.
Creepers explode, and monsters emerge at night wherever it's dark - stated as having always been known, with no one credited for finding it out.
Redstone powers things; people need to eat, sleep, and rest - stated plainly, with no one credited for finding it out.
